messages:
maria_ops: Hey team — customer (ACME corp) is hitting consistent 413s from the embeddings endpoint when they upload a 120k-item batch. They say it used to work with smaller batches. Error from client: `413 Payload Too Large`.

alex_support: thanks for the heads up. do we have a reproduction payload or at least an example size in bytes? 413 usually means > our max request payload size or wrong content-length.

maria_ops: minimal repro: Python requests call sending a JSON array of 120000 vectors (each a float array of length 1536). Rough estimate > 80MB. customer attached snippet:```python
import requests, json
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-XXXXX', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
data = {'model': 'open-embedding-1536', 'input': big_list_of_vectors}
r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=data)
print(r.status_code, r.text)
```

liam_engineer: that size is definitely above our per-request limit. default max payload is 25MB for the hosted embeddings endpoint (internal note). Bulk uploads need to be chunked. Also watch out for dimension mismatch: the model expects vectors as inputs for similarity search in that size; but if user is accidentally sending nested objects it can bloat payloads drastically.

jana_product: can we confirm and give recommended chunking strategy (and an example client pattern) for ACME? They also asked about re-assembly and ordering guarantees.

alex_support: suggested guidance to give customer: 1) split into chunks by byte size (<= 20MB per request) or by item count (~10k vectors depending on dimensions). 2) use sequential POSTs with 'chunk_index' and 'total_chunks' metadata in body or headers to reconstruct on server if they need grouping; 3) use idempotency keys to avoid double-billing on retries.

maria_ops: ACME also reported intermittent dimension mismatch errors: 'expected embedding dim 1536, got 1024' when they changed to a different model variant mid-batch. Could be a routing/fallback scenario.

liam_engineer: yeah, that's important — mixing model types across chunks will cause mismatch at ingest. Our server validates dims on each request; if they plan to migrate models mid-upload they must either: a) re-embed entirely with the new model or b) tag each vector with the model_version it was produced with and store that alongside. We'll add a note to support doc.

sre_bot: @channel automated alert: high 413 rate on /v1/embeddings from customer ACME between 14:20-14:28 UTC. Top clients: acme-ingest-1 (10k reqs), acme-ingest-2 (2k reqs).

alex_support: thanks bot. Maria — please send customer this reproducible chunked upload example (Python) and a curl example they can try quickly:```bash
# chunked by items (send 5000 vectors per request)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"open-embedding-1536","input": [ /* 5000 vectors */ ], "client_chunk_index": 1, "client_total_chunks": 24}'
```

liam_engineer: add retries with exponential backoff and check for `Retry-After` header on 429/503. For 413s we should not retry the same request without shrinking it.

maria_ops: sent example to ACME, they tried splitting to 10k per request and got past the 413 but saw throttling/latency spikes. They asked about throughput tuning/parallelism.

liam_engineer: tradeoff notes: more parallelism increases throughput but also increases backend load and may hit rate limits. Recommend: 1) pick chunk size to keep per-request payload < 20MB, 2) maintain concurrency of ~4-8 workers for sustained uploads, 3) monitor token/byte/service quotas. Also we support streaming NDJSON-style payloads for very large workloads (experimental) — it accepts newline-delimited JSON objects where each line is a single input embedding request; this reduces peak memory on client and can bypass some size limits if the connection stays open and the server handles streaming. We'll check if customer's SDK can use streaming.

jana_product: is the streaming NDJSON documented? we should surface it in the support KB. If experimental, mark as beta and include recommended headers: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson`.

liam_engineer: right. implementation notes for the doc: - server accepts a stream of JSON objects each like `{"id":"uuid-1","vector":[...],"meta":{}}` terminated by newline - server returns per-line success status in a final response or streams per-item status depending on mode - enforce a soft per-connection items limit (e.g., 250k items) and hard max content-bytes/timeouts - require consistent model param across the stream otherwise validation errors for later lines.

maria_ops: ACME tried streaming with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and still hit a `413` after ~30s — their SDK closed and retried, creating duplicate partial uploads. They saw unexpectedly high billing because each successful chunk billed separately.

billing_bot: note: each successful embeddings request is billed independently. Retries without idempotency keys may result in double charges for partially completed uploads. Recommend `Idempotency-Key` header on each chunk.

alex_support: action items for us: 1) reply to ACME with concrete chunking examples + concurrency guidance (done). 2) enable example code for streaming NDJSON in our Python SDK and mark beta. 3) add server-side 413 message to include a hint: e.g., `413 Payload Too Large: try splitting into chunks of <= 20MB or use streaming NDJSON` so customers get actionable text. 4) add docs note about model dim mismatch when mixing models across chunks.

liam_engineer: I'll open a quick internal doc/PR with recommended constants: `MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES=20_000_000`, `RECOMMENDED_ITEMS_PER_CHUNK=5000` (for 1536 dims), `DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY=6`, and examples for calculating bytes per vector. Also add a sample chunker snippet:```python
from math import ceil
MAX_BYTES = 20_000_000
def chunk_vectors(vectors):
    chunks = []
    cur = []
    cur_bytes = 0
    for v in vectors:
        b = len(json.dumps(v).encode('utf-8'))
        if cur and cur_bytes + b > MAX_BYTES:
            chunks.append(cur)
            cur = []
            cur_bytes = 0
        cur.append(v)
        cur_bytes += b
    if cur: chunks.append(cur)
    return chunks
```

maria_ops: perfect. ACME also asked for a quick checklist to avoid common pitfalls — can someone paste a short list?

alex_support: checklist: 1) confirm model dims before sending (match embedding model) 2) chunk by bytes/items to stay < 20MB 3) use `Idempotency-Key` per chunk 4) add exponential backoff and check `Retry-After` 5) prefer streaming NDJSON for very large pipelines but ensure consistent model param across the stream 6) instrument request ids so we can trace on our side (include `x-client-request-id`).

jana_product: I'll get the KB update scheduled. Liam, please add the constants to the internal SDK README and open a small PR for the server message change.

liam_engineer: on it — will post PR link here when ready.

sre_bot: alert resolved — 413 rate returned to baseline after customer switched to chunked uploads.

maria_ops: closing loop with ACME, they verified ingestion completed and costs were reasonable after idempotency keys. thanks all. :tada:
